newsitem.title: UK: Major says UK will rule on BA/American link.
newsitem.headline: Major says UK will rule on BA/American link.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday that the British authorities -- not the European Commission -- would decide wither a proposed alliance between British Airways American Airlines could go ahead.
EC Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert replied that Major's view would be a major problem "unless the British decision would completely satisfy also our competition concerns.
"If that is not the case, then we will have to take the member state to court for ignoring Community law and Community obligations" Van Miert told Reuters Television in Brussels.
Major had earlier replied to an MP's complaint over reports that Van Miert considered the BA-American deal anti-competitive and had told Britain not to give it a green light.
The Commission's views would be taken into account by Britain's Office of Fair Trading, Major told parliament.
But at the end of the day, he said, it would be for Trade and Industry Minister Ian Lang, not the Commission, to decide.
Major also said that he found the Commission's comments "very strange" because the alliance would only go ahead if Britain and the United States agreeed to a related "open skies" trade pact.

Britain and the Commission have been on a collision course over the transatlantic alliance since the Office of Fair Trading announced in December it would clear the deal provided the two airlines agreed to give away 168 weekly takeoff and landing slots at London's congested Heathrow Airport.
BA indicated that it would agree to surrender the slots if it could sell them.
But both Van Miert and European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock have said that slots can only be exchanged or given away, not sold, under EU rules.
The alliance is also being examined by U.S. authorities.

The Commission said earlier on Thursday that the deal would completely eliminate competition on 14 routes between Britain and the United States, including London-Dallas, Birmingham-New-York and Glasgow-Boston.
